history.titleZh: 宏碁 Swift Go 16 AI（AMD Gorgon Point）评测：一款均衡、实惠的大屏便携本
history.descriptionZh:
Acer推出新款Swift Go 16 AI笔记本电脑，定位主流价位的大屏便携机型。评测机型搭载AMD Ryzen AI 7 445处理器（“Gorgon Point”架构），配备16GB LPDDR5X内存、1TB PCIe Gen 4固态硬盘、16英寸1920×1200 IPS触摸屏（120Hz刷新率），以及一块7英寸（对角线）的大面积触控板。整机重约3.53磅（约1.6千克），厚度0.63英寸，采用铝合金外壳，黑色顶盖带有锯齿状细纹，整体质感优于同价位入门产品。接口方面配备两个USB4（Type-C）、两个USB 3.2 Gen 1（Type-A）、HDMI 2.1、microSD卡槽和耳机孔，支持Wi-Fi 7和蓝牙5.4，内置65Wh电池，附带100W USB-C充电器。

这款笔记本最核心的亮点在于其AI能力。Ryzen AI 7 445为6核12线程设计，集成AMD Radeon 840M显卡，NPU算力达到50 TOPS，足以运行Windows 11的Copilot+功能及各类本地AI应用。在生产力性能测试中，Geekbench 6单核成绩略低于戴尔XPS 14（Core Ultra X7 358H），但多核表现反超；Handbrake视频转码测试同样优于XPS 14。不过，面对苹果MacBook Air（M5）和联想Yoga Slim 7x（骁龙X）等Arm架构机型，Acer在能效和转码速度上明显落后——后者将4K视频转1080p只需前者的约三分之一时间。25GB文件传输测试中，Acer的SSD实测速度847.88 MB/s，不到竞争对手的一半，但对日常使用足够。3DMark Steel Nomad图形测试得分为234，约为XPS 14的一半，是MacBook Air和Yoga Slim 7x的四分之一；不过x86平台在游戏兼容性上仍有优势。

屏幕是这台机器的加分项。IPS面板实测亮度336尼特，略高于联想Yoga Slim 7x，但低于戴尔和苹果；色域覆盖121.8% sRGB和86.3% DCI-P3，颜色表现丰富。虽然不如OLED的纯黑对比度，但日常办公和观影完全够用。键盘手感中规中矩，方向键设计略显夸张，且为了塞入数字小键盘导致布局略显局促。7英寸玻璃触控板是该机特色之一，表面覆盖康宁大猩猩玻璃，并支持在打开YouTube、Teams等应用时动态显示背光媒体控制按钮（可调节音量、播放、全屏等），关闭只需点击右下角X。扬声器为向下发声设计，音量和低音一般，附带DTS:X Ultra软件可选EQ预设。电池续航在屏幕150尼特、混合负载测试下达到9.5小时，优于联想Yoga Slim 7x（8.7小时），但不及戴尔和苹果。10轮Cinebench 2026压力测试中，键盘表面最高约100.5°C，底部最高114°C，触摸板区87°C，内部CPU平均温度66.9°C，作为轻薄本可接受。500万像素IR摄像头支持Windows Hello，最高可录制2560×1600视频，色彩准确但细节偏软，对强光有溢出。

评测中还提到一个有趣的问题：笔记本的霍尔传感器对磁场异常敏感，作者右手佩戴的磁吸表带会导致屏幕频繁熄灭并退回登录界面，换左手或摘表后恢复正常，且其他笔记本无此问题，推测是Acer的传感器屏蔽设计不够完善。

可升级性方面，卸下底部十颗Torx螺丝即可打开后盖，可更换M.2 2280固态硬盘和无线网卡，但内存为板载焊接不可升级。预装软件方面，系统内带有一定数量的广告和冗余程序，如Forge of Empires、Dropbox、Booking.com、ExpressVPN等，且AcerSense应用需要手动下载安装，用户可自行卸载。

价格方面，评测的AMD版本在Best Buy售价波动较大：评测期间曾低至799.99美元，而当前MSRP为1,149美元。另有搭载Intel Core Ultra 5 322、512GB存储但换用OLED屏的银色版本，评测时曾降至699美元，性价比极高；高配AMD版（Ryzen 9 465+32GB）为1,499美元，Intel Core Ultra 7 355+32GB版MSRP 1,549美元。总体而言，Swift Go 16 AI在低于800美元时是极具吸引力的大屏AI笔记本，兼顾主流性能、优质IPS屏幕和丰富的接口配置，但若恢复至1,149美元原价则与同价位OLED机型相比竞争力有所下降。该机适合需要大屏幕、长续航、本地AI功能及x86游戏兼容性的用户，尤其是希望以合理预算获得接近高端机型体验的消费者。

history.title: AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin blocking new developments — growing public outrage and bipartisan pushback threaten big tech expansion plans
history.description: New AI data center development bans jumped to over 500 in July, according to recent analysis, with political and public pressure growing.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The number of local bans on new data center developments jumped to over 500 in July, according to recent data. Local politicians in the United States are refusing to approve new data center construction in greater numbers, posing a threat to the expansion required by AI firms to provide the capacity needed to power the new technology. The analysis, conducted by The Information from legal documents and local news reports, shows that this isn’t a partisan issue.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)Photonics and high-speed data movement is the next big AI bottleneckThe data center cooling state of playMassive AI data center buildouts are squeezing energy suppliesUltra Ethernet: The data center interconnection of tomorrowRepublican- and Democrat-run states, towns and counties have all begun to block new data center projects, with Texas and New York both prominent entries from both sides of the political divide, and with the majority of the bans appearing in the Midwest and South, according to the report.Politicians aren’t doing this out of spite, but in response to the growing concern from residents over the impact on communities. Among them are the impact of noise on local residents, as well as the disproportionate impact on public services, including on water and electricity supplies. It follows Texas Governor Greg Abbott’s moratorium on data center approvals in recent weeks until an extensive audit has been conducted of companies looking to hook their new centers up to the Texan power grid.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The Information’s analysis shows that the bans are growing fast, jumping from 300 in late June to over 500 in July. The ban in Texas is particularly noteworthy due to the state becoming a prominent home for AI data centers. Despite Governor Abbott’s pause, Amazon is still hoping to build a new gas power plant in Pecos County, Texas, to power a data center at the same location. That location is already believed to likely become the single biggest source of environmental pollution in the U.S. once it’s operational.The rapid growth of new data centers in Texas and nearby states has likely fueled those concerns from residents. The Information reports that most of the bans are in the Midwest and South, with more than 400 restrictions now in place, with nearly three-quarters of the moratoriums approved in July occurring in southern states like Georgia and Florida. Florida, in particular, is quickly stopping new developments, with 14 out of 23 current active restrictions in that state being approved in July, and 15 more under consideration. You may like 142 AI data center protests staged in 42 states as public opposition increases Over 70% of Americans oppose AI data centers; US protests intensify as more arrests are being made More than 75 data center build-outs worth $130 billion have been successfully blocked in the first three months of 2026 Small and big, rural and urban states alike are all seeing political capital used on preventing AI data center expansion. Kathy Hochul, Democrat Governor of New York, recently signed an executive order that paused approval for all data centers consuming 50 megawatts of energy or more. Massachusetts and Nebraska halted tax breaks for developers, while in Colorado, 19 bans are now in place around Denver, and more elsewhere in the state, due to concerns specifically around the impact on the environment and on water usage. In Nashville, Tennessee, a 23-acre data center development next to a zoo, expected to cost up to $700 million, is also facing local and political resistance.It’s no surprise to see politicians begin to wake up to the public malaise against AI development. history.titleZh: AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin blocking new developments — growing public outrage and bipartisan pushback threaten big tech expansion plans
history.descriptionZh:
美国AI数据中心的扩张正遭遇日益强烈的本地阻力。据The Information对法律文件和地方新闻报道的分析，截至7月，美国各地针对新建数据中心的禁令数量已突破500项，较6月底的约300项急剧增长。这一趋势并非党派之争——共和党和民主党执政的州、城镇和县均在阻止新项目落地，其中得克萨斯州和纽约州是两党对立最明显的代表，而禁令最集中的地区是中西部和南部。

地方政府此举并非出于政治意气，而是对居民关切的直接回应。当地社区普遍担忧数据中心带来的噪音污染，以及其对水电等公共服务资源的过度挤占。得州州长格雷格·阿博特近期已暂停批准新建数据中心，要求对拟接入得州电网的企业进行全面审计。得州已成为AI数据中心的重要聚集地，但该州的抵制尤为引人注目。亚马逊仍计划在得州佩科斯县新建一座天然气发电厂，为当地数据中心供电，而该地点一旦投入运营，预计将成为美国最大的单一环境污染源。

数据中心的快速增长加剧了居民的不满。分析显示，目前中部和南部州份已实施超过400项限制，其中7月批准的禁令中近四分之三来自佐治亚、佛罗里达等南部州。佛罗里达州尤其积极，现有23项限制中有14项于7月获批，另有15项正在审议中。纽约州民主党州长凯西·霍楚尔签署行政令，暂停审批所有耗能50兆瓦及以上的数据中心；马萨诸塞州和内布拉斯加州则取消了针对开发商的税收优惠；科罗拉多州丹佛市周边已实施19项禁令，其他地区也因环境和用水顾虑出台更多限制。田纳西州纳什维尔市一座紧邻动物园、耗资高达7亿美元、占地23英亩的数据中心项目也面临当地政治阻力。

政治人物开始正视公众对AI开发的普遍不满。据统计，超过70%的美国人反对新建更多AI数据中心，针对项目的直接抗议也在增加，今年迄今已有至少37人因抗议新开发项目被捕。这种日益高涨的抵制潮，正在成为AI企业扩张算力基础设施、满足新技术需求所必须面对的重大现实障碍。

history.title: GeForce NOW exploit lets you access the full Windows desktop through a simple file swap — Modder runs local AI models on Ultimate tier with 48GB of VRAM and no restrictions
history.description: Swapping the executable of a game with a modified file will fool Steam into thinking it's opening that game when it's really just giving you unrestricted desktop access. This is against GeForce NOW's terms of service, though, so you run the risk of getting banned.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia's GeForce NOW cloud gaming service has been a popular way to access your games on the go without worrying about hardware. It has a free tier with titles like Fortnite, not even requiring a purchase, but the paid subscription enjoys much better specs and rate limits. As such, using the "Ultimate" tier, modder Zortos was able to gain full access to the Windows desktop inside GeForce NOW, allowing him to use it as a normal computer that can (ironically) run local AI models on it.LM Studio on GeForce NOWGemma 4 31B (41 TPS) on Ultimate Tier pic.twitter.com/kspmKmunFlAugust 7, 2026For context, GeForce NOW is only meant for gaming; Nvidia does not advertise it as a general, all-purpose cloud streamer like Shadow PC, for instance. Hence, doing all this is certainly against the terms of service, and you run the risk of your account getting banned. With that being said, ethically, you are paying for renting hardware, so trying to gain desktop access is predicated on how far your own moral scruples allow you to go.Anyhow, the exploit begins with an I2P (Install-to-Play) game that you download from Steam — Zortos uses Trove. You click on the publisher's name to open the built-in browser, from where you go to your C: drive through the address bar and essentially hijack the index. You open the steamapps folder that was just created for Trove and copy the path of the main executable from the contents.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Zortos on YouTube)This file is replaced with a decoy that deceives Steam into thinking you're actually starting Trove when you click on the "Play" button. In reality, it's a modified executable developed by another modder, dpadGuy, that just opens the desktop instead. Once inside, it really is the full Windows environment with no apparent restrictions. The video below even shows Zortos installing Wallpaper Engine and customizing the taskbar.However, users have reported some discrepancies between their experiences, such as GeForce NOW simply closing the session when it sees the File Explorer open, or the service blocking file downloads, which is a necessary step to replace the executable. Zortos insists that the exploit is still working on his X account, and he even says that if you have persistent storage, the exploit will remain active between different sessions. You may like Chinese modder gets GeForce RTX 4060 working in Windows 11 on Huawei Arm workstation Crazed modder turns NAS into a gaming PC with RTX 5060 hanging from the side, boosts frame rate by 828% AI enthusiast adds Nvidia Tesla V100 as loud as a lawnmower to gaming PC for $266 Keep in mind that you need a paid tier of GeForce NOW to be able to pull this off, and even if you do, it's against Nvidia's ToS as you're not allowed to venture beyond games. Running local AI models on a setup like this doesn't make sense because of the session rate limits, but the Ultimate tier Zortos used does give you access to 48GB of VRAM (thanks to an RTX Pro 6000D) so it might be worthwhile for some. history.titleZh: GeForce NOW exploit lets you access the full Windows desktop through a simple file swap — Modder runs local AI models on Ultimate tier with 48GB of VRAM and no restrictions
history.descriptionZh:
Nvidia的GeForce NOW云游戏服务一直是以低门槛访问游戏库的热门方案，用户无需高性能硬件即可在各类设备上畅玩。该服务提供免费层级（可无需购买直接游玩《堡垒之夜》等游戏），而付费订阅则享有更高规格的虚拟机配置和更宽松的使用限制。就在近期，一位名叫Zortos的模组作者利用“Ultimate”终级付费层级，成功突破了GeForce NOW仅限游戏的限制，获得了完整的Windows桌面访问权限，并讽刺性地在这台“云电脑”上运行起了本地AI模型。他在X平台发布视频，展示了通过LM Studio运行Gemma 4 31B模型，在Ultimate层级上达到每秒41 tokens（41 TPS）的速度。

需要明确的是，GeForce NOW本质上是为游戏而生的流媒体服务，Nvidia从未像Shadow PC那样将其定位为通用云计算平台。因此，这种越界行为明显违反了服务条款（ToS），账号随时可能被永久封禁。从道德层面看，用户确实是在付费租用硬件，但能否接受这种“越界”取决于个人对服务条款的底线判断。

**技术原理与破解步骤**：Zortos的漏洞利用起始于一款Steam平台的“安装即玩”（I2P）游戏——他使用的是《Trove》。具体流程如下：首先下载该游戏，然后点击发行商名称以打开内置浏览器；在浏览器地址栏中导航到C盘根目录，从而“劫持”文件索引；接着打开刚刚为《Trove》创建的steamapps文件夹，复制主执行文件的路径。随后，这个原始文件被替换成一个“诱饵”版本，用于欺骗Steam——当用户点击“Play”按钮时，Steam以为自己启动的是《Trove》，实际上运行的却是另一位模组作者dpadGuy修改过的可执行文件，该文件会直接打开Windows桌面。一旦进入桌面，就是一个看似毫无限制的完整Windows环境。Zortos甚至在视频中展示了安装Wallpaper Engine、自定义任务栏等操作。

不过，其他用户的尝试反馈存在差异。部分人报告GeForce NOW检测到文件资源管理器打开时就强制关闭会话，或者服务端阻止了文件下载——而这正是替换执行文件所必需的步骤。尽管如此，Zortos坚持表示该漏洞仍在他的账号上有效，并声称如果启用了持久化存储，漏洞效果可以跨会话保留。

**性能参数与硬件规格**：值得注意的是，这一操作需要付费订阅GeForce NOW才能实现。Ultimate层级提供了相当可观的云硬件：得益于一块RTX Pro 6000D专业显卡，用户拥有高达48GB的显存。正是这个显存容量让本地运行Gemma 4 31B这类大型语言模型成为可能。然而，由于云游戏服务有严格的会话时长限制，长周期AI推理任务在这种环境中并不实用。但对于某些轻量级、短时的AI实验来说，这确实提供了一个独特的资源通道。

**影响与应用场景**：从技术影响力来看，这次破解再次证明了云游戏平台的算力池拥有远超游戏场景的通用计算潜力。它可能激发更多模组开发者探索类似边界，同时也会促使Nvidia加强风控措施。对于普通用户而言，这更是一个警示——突破服务条款使用云服务不仅面临账号风险，而且受限于会话速率和平台检测，实际应用价值有限。不过，若确实有紧急需求，利用Ultimate层级的48GB VRAM运行临时AI模型，至少为技术爱好者提供了一个有趣的备选方案。当然，最稳妥且合规的方式仍是使用Nvidia官方允许的AI平台或租赁专用云服务器。与此同时，社区中还有诸如“在华为Arm工作站为RTX 4060装上Windows 11”、“将NAS改装成RTX 5060游戏主机”、“为游戏PC加装价值266美元且噪音堪比割草机的Tesla V100”等类似的硬件改造趣闻，共同展现了玩家群体对突破硬件用途界限的持续热情。

history.title: Over 70% of Americans oppose AI data centers; US protests intensify as more arrests are being made — almost 40 arrested this year in backlash to AI factory buildout
history.description: The public pushback against data center construction projects is only growing stronger, even as some protesting local residents have been arrested in the process.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The public pushback against data center construction projects is only growing stronger, even as some protesting local residents have been arrested in the process. That hasn't perturbed those still standing against the AI infrastructure projects, though, and they continue showing up at town meetings, holding protest rallies, and making themselves heard — even with the 24/7 drone of a data center hum in the background.The latest effort saw Nashville residents and local politicians move to block the construction of a $700 million data center set to be built right next to the Nashville Zoo at Grassmere. The city council approved a blocking measure last week, and now Mayor Freddie O'Connell will wield it to make sure the project doesn't go ahead.This follows on from another recent story where a Kentucky farming family was offered 10 times their land value to sell up to data center developers, and they refused. Virginia's State Corporation Commission, which regulates public utilities, just ruled that data centers must pay for all the required transmission infrastructure that they have exclusive use of, in an effort to reduce energy bills for residents.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Nobody wants to live near a data centerData center projects have been firmly disliked by large bodies of Americans since the beginning of this major AI buildout. Early in 2025, it became clear that even as the major AI companies were promising hundreds of billions for "AI factories," governments around the world rushed to build capacity. There was only one problem: residents near the proposed build sites would not be taking it lying down.In April 2025, Elon Musk's Colossus data center was an early target for protest after it was found to be using permitless mobile gas turbines for power. It's been hit with enough pushback since then that SpaceX has now agreed to remove the 69 turbines it ultimately installed, although it is going to take over a year to complete the move of these allegedly mobile turbines. You may like 70% of Americans oppose data centers near their homes, now less popular than nuclear power plants At least 37 people arrested in 2026 so far for protesting against data centers, most for breaking 'petty rules' AI data center bans surge past 500 nationwide as local US politicians begin quickly blocking new developments By the Fall of last year, evidence had begun to mount about the negative impact of these installations. Water shortages and potential contamination, electricity price increases for residents, and the constant, unending noise that may be causing health problems with sub-audible frequencies.There's also the slowly growing number of "against" voices in polling for new data centers. What started as a light advantage to the "supports" respondents in September became a near-majority a few months later. Now more than 70% of Americans don't want data centers near their homes, and there's little chance of that changing as the stories of issues during and after construction of these facilities continue to mount.How the people are fighting backProtest has been at the forefront of the anti-data center campaigners' playbook since the start, and that's not stopping any time soon. On one weekend in July, anti-data center protestors organized in 42 states to stage 142 protests across the country, all calling for blocks, halts, and moratoriums on the data center rollout.This is after months of campaigning, which led to close to 70 jurisdictions around the country blocking new data center builds. Some of them, permanently.Where politicians are more on the side of the developers, the people are going to meet them in person. They're going to town halls and seeking meetings and making their voices heard. What to read next 142 AI data center protests staged in 42 states as public opposition increases More than 75 data center build-outs worth $130 billion have been successfully blocked in the first three months of 2026 Pennsylvania residents complain they are being 'bulldozed' over AI data center concerns Sometimes politicians don't like that, and people are removed - even when protesting peacefully - and in several cases they've actually been arrested. Close to 40 people have been arrested in 2026 for pushing back against data center rollouts. In one case, because they went beyond their allotted speaking time, and in another, because they clapped following an impassioned statement by a fellow citizen.In other cases, though, politicians are listening. In Nashville, the local council and the mayor are all on board to protect the local Zoo and residents' bills and ears. This is particularly important because it shows that local legislators can use their political power to block data centers — potentially preventing the White House from using its own to drive projects through.The forever warThe data center builders aren't taking all of this helplessly. They have the ears of government and massive platforms to evangelize AI and data centers; They've been doing it everywhere from the White House to social media. They've tried building in more rural areas where there are fewer people to protest, paying for their own behind-the-grid power, and offering to spend millions in local investment to counter negative effects.But it's not working. People don't like data centers. They don't want to live near them. And on top of that, many don't even like the technology the hyperscalers want to build this all for, anyway.It's unlikely that those bankrolling (and hoping to make money on) the data center AI build-out will just give up and go home, but the residents fighting back against their gargantuan construction projects aren't going to do so either.This is a long war, and one that neither side is likely to back down from. But in a rare ray of hope in 2026's landscape of high PC and electronics prices due to AI data centers soaking up computing hardware, it's one that the people seem to be winning, for now.

history.titleZh: 超70%美国人反对AI数据中心；美国抗议升级，逮捕人数增加——今年已有近40人因反对AI工厂建设被捕
history.descriptionZh:
美国各地针对人工智能数据中心建设项目的民间抵制正在持续升级，且已从零散抗议演变为有组织的政治行动。近期最典型的案例发生在田纳西州纳什维尔：该市议会通过一项阻止令，否决了拟建在纳什维尔动物园旁、投资达7亿美元的数据中心项目，市长弗雷迪·奥康奈尔将动用行政权力确保该项目无法推进。这一决定被视为地方政府利用立法工具对抗AI基建扩张的标志性胜利。

在此之前，肯塔基州一个农场家庭拒绝了开发商以土地价值10倍报价收购其土地用于数据中心建设的要求；弗吉尼亚州公用事业监管机构则裁定，数据中心必须为其独占使用的全部输电基础设施买单，以减轻普通居民的能源账单负担。

自大型AI建设浪潮启动以来，数据中心项目在美国公众中的反对声浪日渐高涨。2025年初，各大AI公司承诺投入数千亿美元建设“AI工厂”，各国政府也竞相扩大算力产能，但拟建工地附近的居民并未坐视不理。2025年4月，埃隆·马斯克的“Colossus”数据中心因使用无许可证的移动燃气轮机供电而成为首批抗议目标，SpaceX最终同意拆除其安装的69台涡轮机，但迁移动作预计耗时超过一年。

反对的理由集中在实际危害上：水资源短缺与污染风险、居民电价上涨，以及持续不断、可能包含次声波频率的噪音，被指对健康造成影响。民调数据也明显转向：2025年9月支持者还略占优势，几个月后反对者已接近半数，如今超过70%的美国人表示不希望数据中心建在自己家附近。随着建设和运营期间的问题不断曝光，这一趋势预计将继续恶化。

民众的反击手段以抗议为主，且规模越来越大。2025年7月的一个周末，反数据中心抗议者在42个州组织了142场示威，呼吁全面叫停、暂停和限制数据中心建设。经过数月行动，全国已有近70个辖区对新建数据中心实施封锁，部分为永久禁令。在政治人物偏向开发商的地区，民众直接前往市政厅会议和听证会发声，有时即使和平抗议也会被驱逐甚至逮捕——2026年以来已有约37人因抗议被捕，其中有人因超时发言，有人因在他人发言后鼓掌。

不过也有政治人物选择倾听民意。纳什维尔市议会和市长一致决定保护当地动物园、居民账单和安静环境，表明地方政府完全有能力利用权力阻止数据中心，从而制衡白宫层面推动项目的压力。

数据中心开发商并未坐以待毙。他们依托政府关系和庞大的媒体平台持续宣传AI和数据中心的必要性，尝试在人口稀少的农村地区建设以减少抗议人群，自建电网供电，并承诺投入数百万美元地方投资来补偿负面影响。但这些策略收效甚微。公众对数据中心的反感已根深蒂固，许多人甚至对整个超大规模AI技术本身持怀疑态度。

尽管这场拉锯战远未结束——出资方不会轻易放弃AI建设可能带来的巨额回报，反抗的居民也绝不会退缩——但在2026年AI数据中心因抢占算力硬件而推高PC和电子产品价格的背景下，这场持续已久的战争中，民众暂时占据了上风。
